islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel scent
channel bad
channel value
channel dark
channel front
channel injection

# how much unknown lies around a cell: a smoothed field of not-yet-known cells
rule darkness:
  when 1
  set dark = 0.5 * (1 - free) * (1 - solid) + 0.5 * avg8(dark)

# the frontier part of source: faint marks where no smell and no morsel are painted
rule split:
  when 1
  set front = where(scent + thing < 0.05, source, 0)

# food counts as told; a frontier counts by the darkness behind it; tight places count less
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(source - front, thing * (1 - bad), front * (0.3 + 2.0 * dark)) / (1 + 0.5 * sum8(solid))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.

channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (0.9941 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.7182 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

observations.text:
The agent spends its whole life inside one small walled pocket (a 4x12 box, start and death in the same spot), sweeping back and forth along it and never leaving, so it never even reaches the food lying a short walk away in the neighbouring rooms.
It does press and break things (3 doors, 5 breaks), but after each press it drifts back into the pocket instead of walking through, so the openings it makes do not turn into a route out.
The failure is that inside a sealed pocket every boundary cell is known solid, so there are no frontier marks (unknown cells touching known-free ones) and the value field has nothing to point at except leak through walls, which is weak and spread evenly around the whole box.
A fix: give solid cells that have unknown space behind them (a wall with darkness on its far side, especially one whose leak was taught high by a door opening) a source of their own when no frontier exists, so the wave leads the agent into one specific wall and through it, and keep that target (a lingering source) until it is passed.

turns.hypothesis: Every frontier mark is worth the same 0.12 today, so a one-cell unknown pocket beside a wall pulls as hard as the edge of a large unexplored region. Weighting each frontier mark by the smoothed amount of unknown around it (information gain) sends the agent toward big unseen areas where new food is likely, while smell and seen morsels keep their value and the confinement suppression is kept.

A reactive wave lets the agent step back onto the cell it just left whenever two targets are nearly equal, which wastes ticks in back-and-forth limit cycles. A fading footprint channel (trail = max(here, decay*trail), scrolling with the map) dims what the agent READS on its own recent path while the plan wave itself stays untouched, so it commits forward and sweeps instead of dithering, but can still return when the way back is clearly better.

One discount serves two different promises: food (certain, worth a detour only when near) and the frontier (uncertain, but only informative if the agent commits to a long walk). Splitting the wave into an exploitation wave with a steep discount and an exploration wave with a shallow discount, read as their max, lets far frontiers keep a coherent long-range pull while nearby food still wins when close.

When frontiers on several sides look alike, the agent's target can switch from thought to thought and it sweeps nothing completely. A frozen random preference per place (seeded once, inherited by cells scrolling in, smoothed into regions, and carried with the map) breaks such ties the same way every thought, so the agent commits to one side of the unknown and explores it through; the frontier/food split is also computed inline now, removing a one-pass lag that injected a stale full-strength peak.

Exploration is driven only by frontier marks, which exist only where unknown ground touches known-free ground; once the agent has seen every wall of a room, cave or pocket, the value field has nothing to aim at and it sweeps the box until it starves (the observer's world-16 life). A BREACH source on every reachable wall cell with darkness behind it, weighted by the darkness and passed through the wall's taught leak, is weak enough that any food or frontier beats it in the max, but when nothing else calls it leads the agent into the most promising wall, where pressing opens doors and chips rubble; stone that never gives is taught a low leak and drops out, so the agent tries walls in turn. Food in this world grows on fixed spots that regrow on a timer, yet every law so far forgets a spot as soon as its sighting fades, so the agent re-finds food only by luck. A long LARDER memory of where good morsels were seen, multiplied by a RIPENESS clock that is reset whenever the agent stands on or beside the place and climbs slowly back, injects a source that calls the agent back to a patch about when it should have regrown: a trapline over the remembered map, on top of the darkness-weighted frontier and the footprint trail.
